market.headline: Uptrend, narrow participation
market.read: The index is above both its 50- and 200-day averages with the 50 above the 200 — an uptrend by every conventional definition. Breadth is mixed — 43 of 87 tracked names above their own 50-day. The index is holding up while most individual names are not, which means the average is being carried by a few of them. Long bonds and high-yield credit are both down over 60 sessions: conditions tightening and risk appetite retreating together.

macro.headline: Rates rising and credit widening together
macro.short: Long bonds and high-yield credit are both down over 60 sessions: conditions tightening and risk appetite retreating together.
macro.read: Long bonds down 4.7% and high-yield credit down 3.1% over 60 sessions. Both proxies moving against risk at once is the most straightforwardly hostile of the four backdrops: money is getting more expensive and simultaneously harder to borrow. Nothing here is specific to any one ticker — it is the weather every position is being held in.
macro.caveat: TLT and HYG are proxies for rates and credit, not measurements of them — each carries its own duration, supply and fund-flow effects. Sixty sessions of realised moves, and nothing here forecasts the next sixty.

market.caveat: A description of the tape as it stands, measured across the 87 tickers this site tracks — not a forecast, and 87 names is not the whole market.
